summary: Accepted the bounded single-app proof that the actual counter module and encoder selected from the frozen React-profile manifest run in a DOM-only Chromium bundle. Metafile inputs, raw state/DOM observations, guard results, and stable source pins substantiate the claim. The invalid historical worker-receipt enum is preserved and the current receipt is corrected; no full matrix or same-session renderer swap is accepted here.

review_findings.compiled_input: The manifest identifies the frozen React-profile counter package; AppIR roles map to exported compiled Init/Update/View symbols. The exact module and matching encoder are esbuild inputs.
review_findings.browser_run: Chromium recorded Init 0, Add 1, Add 2, Reset 0; reset-disabled followed 0/positive/0; trace messages were add/add/reset with four ticks.
review_findings.independence_guards: The preserved run records empty WebAssembly API, Fetch, XHR, WASM resource, page-error, and unhandled-rejection lists; only the local page and one bundle were requested.
review_findings.source_pins: The run JSON has identical before/after pin sets for the manifest, AppIR, module, encoder, DOM renderer, runtime, shared view code, map data, and proof script. The current runtime hash equals the recorded dcc4 pin.
review_findings.status_history: The invalid original receipt outcome is preserved byte-for-byte in history; the current receipt uses confirmed_reuse. The run JSON's passed decision is a separate run result. No proof files changed during the metadata correction.

limits: Accepted scope is one counter DOM-only boot and four-step action run only.
The static react-map.gen.mjs data file is present by design; there are no React or ReactDOM packages, adapters, or external imports.
No same-session React/DOM swap, cross-backend focus test, four-app/five-fixture integration matrix, or universal API/network security claim is made.
No new browser run was performed; the source pin, raw run, and bundle metadata answered the review questions.
